verdict_note: Based on reading only: no build and no tests were run. The session half of P3 holds. Session::save_to_with_entry writes a cloned copy of the held entries through the unchanged save_inner path (same guard, same compare, same origin bookkeeping). A plain save still passes &self.quarantined. A refusal before the write changes nothing, and the session's entries, revision and history stay as they were. The P2 group step restores the layers, the vector entry and the text entry together for every refusal that comes before a write. Undo and redo stay correct under LIFO order: swap_entry records the bytes that are current at undo time, so text records that other commands wrote outside the history survive. The 14 rows and the variable engine are typed, bounded and undoable, and the cuts match STU-DS-133. Two defects should be fixed before the bundled run. F1 (P3): the save drops design file states that a reopened document can still reach. Their children are only child ids, and moving a child out and back (or grouping and ungrouping) gives the same ids again. After reopen the instance reads unknown and refuses commands. The fix is a narrow predicate change. F3 (HOST INTEGRATION): every committed variable command is recorded, attributed and evented as layer.set_tiles_and_entry / STUDIO_VECTOR_PATH_EDITED, and its undo name is `<op> vector`. F2 answers the coordinator's question and needs a lead decision: design-state compaction inside the undo step is feasible. Also, room_for already blocks every sync of a component with 513 or more instances, in the session and after reopen. F4 to F9 are low.

findings.certainty: READ (mechanism); not run. UNVERIFIED: that a child moved out of an instance group and back keeps its index in doc.layers, which content() reads. Group then ungroup of two children relies on the same mechanism.
findings.severity: medium (data loss across save and reopen: an edited design file instance reads `unknown` and refuses every instance command)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/design/persist.rs:360-373 (design_save_entry keeps a state only when s.content_signature == content(doc, layer)); :352-358 (doc claim: a reopened document 'can never return to a state of content its layer no longer draws'); :112-114 (content(): child ids in doc.layers order); :327-331 (design_opened keeps design file states as saved, R2); crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/design/instance.rs:794-819 (instance_record: a design file instance with no entry state for its content reads `import` only at the import signature, else `unknown`)
findings.what: P3 drops every design file state whose content is not the instance's current content. The content signature is only the list of child layer ids. A document with no history can come back to such a list without undo: move a child out of the instance group and back, or group two children and ungroup them. Before this lane, design_opened kept such a state as saved (R2), so the instance read `edited` again once its children were back. Now the saved file no longer holds the state. After reopen the instance reads `unknown` (design_state_absent) and refuses design.instance.* until the design file is imported again. Its variant, property and override edits are lost. The states a redraw supersedes, which P3 is about, always name copy layers that the redraw deleted. Pruning only states that name an absent layer bounds the entry just as well. The 'can never return' doc line is a V4-07 claim with no proving test.
findings.scenario: 1. Import fig-components-autolayout.fig and run design.instance.switch_variant on an instance. The state S is stored for content [c1, c2]. 2. Drag c2 out of the instance group to the root. The content is now [c1], so the instance reads `unknown` in the session, as it did before this lane. 3. Save, close, reopen, and drag c2 back into the group. At b57c82d1: the content [c1, c2] matches S, so the instance reads `edited` with the switched variant. At 9ccbcca8: S was left out of the save, so the instance reads `unknown` and its commands refuse.
findings.fix: At save, prune a state only when one of its content_signature ids is not a layer of the document. Those copies were deleted by a redraw, and no command can bring them back once the history is gone. Keep states whose child ids all still exist. Reword the persist.rs:354-358 claim to that rule. Lead question 2: should the same predicate replace design_opened's native rule (R2, from before this lane)?
findings.test: viewer_design_history.rs, new test a_design_file_state_whose_children_still_exist_survives_save: switch a variant, move one child of the instance to the root, save, reopen, move it back, then assert that inspect.state is `edited` with the switched variant. a_design_file_state_superseded_in_the_session_is_left_out_of_the_save_only stays green, because a variant switch deletes the old copies.

findings.certainty: READ; not run. The builder's figure ('about 511 syncs at two states per sync') was not reproduced. By reading, Redraw::new uses salt = doc.layers.len() (instance.rs:443), and mint_layer_id takes the lowest free id at or above it (layers.rs:51-62). A sync can therefore re-mint the copy ids that the sync before last deleted. push_state (persist.rs:219-227) then replaces that state, and the entry may level off at about 3 states per instance. Defect (1) holds either way.
findings.severity: medium (component sync's binding limit once P2 lifted the text cap; components with many instances can never sync)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/design/instance.rs:1121 (persist::room_for(entry, jobs.len()) before the step); persist.rs:208-214 (room_for: held + more > MAX_PERSISTED_STATES, with no credit for replaced states); persist.rs:219-227 (push_state replaces the same layer, content and instance); instance.rs:1176-1201 (one state per job, written after the step and outside the history); component.rs:770-795 (sync_instances: one job per edited native instance); hsk-studio-folio/src/design_state.rs:67 (MAX_DESIGN_STATES 1024); vector/style.rs MAX_ENTRY_INSTANCES 1024
findings.what: (1) room_for refuses when held + N > 1024 for a component with N instances, and every instance holds at least one state. A component with 513 or more instances (authoring allows 1024) is therefore refused design_state_over_cap on its FIRST sync. Save and reopen do not help: design_opened leaves one state per instance, so 2N > 1024 again. From 342 instances, only one sync per session works. The P2 test uses N = 2, so the claim that 'the per-session sync cap is gone' holds only for small components. (2) Answer to the lead's question: superseded native states can be compacted inside the undo step, the same way the text records are. The design entry becomes a third entry of restructure_and_entries. Each job's state is computed before the commit, against component::project(doc, writes) and the authored records that native_redraw already builds. The step drops each redrawn (layer, instance)'s states whose content the step deletes. Undo swaps the entry back and redo swaps it forward. Under LIFO the swap semantics also keep the design-entry writes that .fig commands make outside the history (same analysis as for text). Costs: (a) about 60-100 lines in instance.rs and persist.rs, because write_design_state splits into build and validate against a projected document and receipt, and room_for counts net new states; (b) the post-commit rollback at instance.rs:1193 disappears, which also closes F5; (c) each sync step holds a third whole-entry snapshot on an undo stack with no cap (up to 1024 states of JSON, roughly 0.3-1 MB per step), so memory grows linearly in long sync loops; (d) design file instances still accumulate, because design_command writes its entries outside the history (R1). The same treatment there (vector, text and design entries in one group) would also end .fig text compaction at reopen; (e) the P3 prune at save then matters for .fig states only.
findings.scenario: (1) design_doc with a rectangle-only component (no text: the text entry caps at 256 layers). Run component.create_instance 513 times; each passes room_for(held, 1). Then component.sync_instances is refused design_state_over_cap, and it is refused again after save and reopen. (2) To measure the builder's figure against the re-minting reading: take the two-instance label from viewer_design_history and print states(design entry) every 50 syncs.
findings.fix: Lead decision (lead question 1). The minimum: room_for counts only the states the write adds after push_state's replacement. Recommended: put the design entry in the sync's group step and compact there the states that step supersedes (costs above), with a byte budget for the history or a DRIVE_LIMITS line. Name the bound that remains in the manual.
findings.test: viewer_design_history.rs: a_513_instance_component_syncs (sync once, then again after save and reopen); thousand_syncs_keep_the_design_entry_bounded (2 instances, 1000 syncs; the state count stops growing); undo_across_a_compacting_sync_restores_the_design_entry_byte_for_byte, plus redo.

findings.certainty: READ; not run. Each hole needs a refusal after the first write: a cancel token set during the step (sticky: the run then refuses everything, so the result cannot be saved), a host CommitPort or admission refusal of the rollback, or total_too_large (512 MiB entry budget). findings.severity: low (the group step is atomic for every refusal before a write; three narrow holes, partly in code that predates this lane)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/harness.rs:1509-1568 (restructure_and_entries; the rollback at :1545-1550 ignores the result of `let _ = run.quietly(Self::undo)` and then reports the entry's code); harness.rs:2538-2552 (history_step chronicle arm: when the inverse applies but the entry swap is refused, it returns without pushing the step on either stack); harness.rs:927-969 (group_step re-applies the inner steps already done, regroups, and reports history_group_failed with restored=true); harness.rs:501-535 and :689-704 (one record and one frame per inner history_step)
findings.what: Judged against the ruling's 'truly atomic': (a) Commit. A refused text write restores the entries already written and undoes the structure step. If that undo is refused too, the structure step and the vector entry stay committed and the saved redo history is dropped (keeping_redo restores it only when no step is left). The command still reports the text write's code, so the refusal claims nothing changed while the layers did. (b) Undo and redo. The inner steps run one at a time. If the restructure step's chronicle inverse applies but its vector swap is refused, history_step drops that step from both stacks. group_step then re-applies the text step and regroups what is left. The result: the layers are reverted, the vector entry still holds the post-sync bytes, the group holds only the text step, and history_group_failed is reported as restored. (c) One user undo of a sync writes two `undo` records, two observe frames and two HISTORY_UNDONE events with two correlations. The lane's host_integration declares one terminal frame per command. (b) and (c) are the shared group_step and history_step behaviour that motion commands also use, and P2 now depends on it. An EntryRestore chain would have the same holes. Only a single step that pre-checks and then swaps every entry closes (b).
findings.scenario: (a) The run token is cancelled after restructure_and_entry_step commits and before the text write. The text write is refused `canceled`, and so is the rollback undo. Copies drawn without text records stay, and the reply says `canceled`. (b) A sync is undone while its vector swap is refused: the split described above.
findings.fix: In history_step, pre-check every swap the step will make before submit_inverse: a cancel check plus a Session dry-run fit of all restores (document_entries_fit over the step's tokens). In restructure_and_entries, check that all entries fit before restructure_and_entry_step commits. When the rollback undo is refused, report history_rollback_failed and name the split. Optionally, inner steps of a group record quietly, so a group undo writes one record and one frame. Or the lead accepts (b) and (c) as the motion-command precedent (lead question 4).
findings.test: A Run-level test under cfg(test) or test-faults: refuse the second entry write after the structure commit, then assert that the undo depth, the layers and both entries are unchanged and the redo history is kept. For a group undo with a refused vector swap, assert that both stacks still hold the whole group.

answers.grouped_step_atomic: Partly. Commit: a refused further entry puts the written entries back and undoes the structure step, so every refusal before a write is clean. A refused rollback undo is ignored (F4a). Undo and redo: group_step re-applies the inner steps already done when a later one is refused, which is correct for a chronicle refusal. One branch is not: an inverse that applies followed by a refused entry swap drops the inner step (history_step, from before this lane), and the group splits (F4b). An EntryRestore chain would have the same hole. Under LIFO the whole-entry text snapshot is safe beside the text writes made outside the history (place_text, live text, .fig redraws, design_opened), because swap_entry records the bytes current at undo time and redo brings them back.
answers.design_state_compaction: Feasible for native instances at moderate cost (F2): the design entry becomes the third entry of the group, each state is computed against the projected document before the commit, the step drops the states it supersedes, and room_for counts net states. Costs: about 60-100 lines; a third whole-entry snapshot per step on an undo stack with no cap; .fig instances unchanged unless design_command moves into the step too. Independently, room_for already blocks components with 513 or more instances.
answers.entries_changed: As built, the session stays dirty after a pruned save while it holds the full entry (pinned at session_contract.rs:3277). That is consistent at the session level, where a plain Session::save would write different bytes. But Viewer::save writes the same pruned bytes again, so the flag stays true after every save for the rest of the session. No product code reads is_dirty today: the native host's unsaved dot reads the undo stack (native-host gui/mod.rs:526). Lead question 3.
answers.p3_requirements: Normal save byte-identical: yes, by reading (held = None writes &self.quarantined), and session_contract's equal-entry case proves the copy path writes the plain bytes. Session entries and history unchanged: yes (a copy; Run pushes no step). entries_changed: see above. Failed or canceled save: same atomic path. Pre-cancel and precheck failures are tested; a mid-stream cancel and a verify failure after the rename are not. After a failure that follows the rename, the pruned file is on disk and the origin has moved, as with save_to. Reopen gives the pruned entry: yes, tested. The prune rule itself: F1.
answers.p2_requirements: 300 syncs never refuse: yes for N = 2 only (F2). Undo across a compaction restores the text byte for byte: yes, for 5 syncs. Text and vector in one step: yes. Redo: yes. Missing: the failure branch (F4) and the design entry (F2).
answers.cuts: Honest against STU-DS-133. Implemented: 12 of its commands plus the 2 of STU-DS-132. Cut and declared: variable_collection.extend, variable.values_by_mode_for_collection, variable.remove_override_for_mode (Folio refuses is_extension), EXPRESSION (StudioValue has no such variant, so it is refused parameter_invalid), the binding commands (rebound is always 0, so STU-DS-132's re-resolution is vacuous), and the async read forms. Not named in the cut list: variable.create by collection reference (id only). Design file variables cannot be read (F7).

lead_questions: F2 (the coordinator's item): adopt in-step design-state compaction for native syncs now, at the cost given in F2, or only fix room_for's net count and declare the bound? Should design_command (.fig redraws) also move its vector, text and design writes into the step (this ends R1)?

F1: does P3's 'superseded' mean 'content differs from the current content' (as built) or 'content names a layer the document no longer holds'? Should the same predicate replace design_opened's native rule (R2)?
entries_changed after a pruned save: stay dirty (as built and pinned by a test) or clean, since Viewer::save would write the same bytes?

F4: accept the shared group_step/history_step holes (a split on a refused swap after the inverse; two records and frames per undo) as the motion-command precedent, or require a pre-checked single-step multi-entry restore before landing?

F3: mapping STUDIO_VARIABLE_SET touches harness-core harness.rs (already touched) and the kernel-bindings DESCRIPTOR (not owned). Do it in this lane, and fix the components lane's commit_records the same way?
Undo-name convention for design rows: underscored op plus the entry token (components, variables, proof) or the catalog id (layout rows)?
